stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module. Let $x \in R$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim(\text{Supp}(M)) \leq 1$, and
\item $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Write
$\text{Supp}(M) = \{\mathfrak m, \mathfrak q_1, \ldots, \mathfrak q_t\}$.
Then
$$
e_R(M, 0, x) =
\sum\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, t}
\text{ord}_{R/\mathfrak q_i}(x)
\text{length}_{R_{\mathfrak q_i}}(M_{\mathfrak q_i}).
$$

A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Let $\varphi : M \to M$ be an endomorphism and $n > 0$
such that $\varphi^n = 0$ and such that $\Ker(\varphi)/\Im(\varphi^{n - 1})$
has finite length as an $R$-module.
Then
$$
e_R(M, \varphi^i, \varphi^{n - i}) = 0
$$
for $i = 0, \ldots, n$.

has finite length as an $R$-module.

reason: Establishes finite quotient lengths and derives symmetric lengths by exact sequences and recurrences for the kernel filtration.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A $2$-periodic complex $(M,N,\varphi,\psi)$ over $R$ consists of maps $\varphi:M\to N$ and $\psi:N\to M$ with $\psi\varphi=0=\varphi\psi$. Its two cohomology modules are $H^0=\ker\varphi/\operatorname{im}\psi$ and $H^1=\ker\psi/\operatorname{im}\varphi$. When both have finite length, $e_R(M,N,\varphi,\psi)=\operatorname{length}_R H^0-\operatorname{length}_R H^1$. A $(2,1)$-periodic complex $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ is the special case $M=N$.

Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$(M, \varphi, \psi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$
with $M$ finite and with cohomology groups of finite length over $R$.
Let $x \in R$ be such that $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$. Then
$$
e_R(M, x\varphi, \psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) - e_R(\Im(\varphi), 0, x)
$$
and
$$
e_R(M, \varphi, x\psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) + e_R(\Im(\psi), 0, x)
$$
hypotheses:
Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$(M, \varphi, \psi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$
with $M$ finite and with cohomology groups of finite length over $R$.
Let $x \in R$ be such that $\dim(\text{Supp}(M/xM)) \leq 0$.
conclusions:
$$
e_R(M, x\varphi, \psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) - e_R(\Im(\varphi), 0, x)
$$
and
$$
e_R(M, \varphi, x\psi) = e_R(M, \varphi, \psi) + e_R(\Im(\psi), 0, x)
$$

reason: Removes x-power torsion by additivity and computes the multiplicity difference from the stated exact sequence when x is injective; the second formula is analogous.
